ORVEX is an intelligent Mars exploration and astronaut safety system that combines NASA's open planetary data with an autonomous six-legged robot, HEX-01, to support safer navigation across the Martian surface.

We developed an interactive mission-control platform that integrates NASA datasets, including MOLA, THEMIS, HiRISE, and CTX, to analyze terrain characteristics, surface roughness, thermal conditions, and potential hazards.

HEX-01 is designed to explore challenging terrain, scan the surrounding environment, and assess ground stability, slope, hardness, and obstacles. Using physics and mechanical principles, ORVEX analyzes these conditions and generates a digital hazard map that classifies areas as safe, caution, or dangerous.

The platform also demonstrates intelligent route planning, dynamic replanning, and astronaut safety monitoring through an interactive simulation.

Our innovation bridges the gap between orbital observations and ground-level verification**, transforming NASA data into actionable information for safer exploration.

ORVEX aims to reduce exploration risks, improve mission efficiency, and support future human missions to Mars.
details:
ORVEX – Intelligent Mars Exploration and Astronaut Safety System

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Challenge: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

Project Overview

ORVEX is an intelligent Mars exploration and astronaut safety system designed to improve navigation and reduce risks during future human missions to Mars.

Our project combines NASA's real planetary datasets, an interactive mission-control platform, physics-based analysis, and a physically developed six-legged robotic prototype called HEX-01.

The main objective is to bridge the gap between orbital observations and ground-level verification, helping astronauts make safer and more informed exploration decisions.

How Does ORVEX Work?

ORVEX begins by integrating real NASA planetary data through NASA Mars Trek, focusing on the Jezero Crater region.

The platform incorporates several important datasets:

MOLA: Provides topographic information and surface roughness context.

THEMIS: Provides thermal infrared imagery for understanding surface conditions.

HiRISE and CTX: Provide high-resolution orbital imagery for terrain inspection.

CRISM: Provides mineralogical information supporting scientific exploration.

USGS Geological Maps: Provide geological context for identifying scientifically valuable locations.

These datasets help establish an understanding of the Martian environment and support preliminary mission planning.

Our HEX-01 robotic prototype represents the ground-verification component of the system.

HEX-01 features six articulated legs powered by 18 servo motors, two ultrasonic sensors for obstacle detection, and a custom-designed, 3D-printed mechanical structure.

Its hexapod configuration was selected to improve mobility and stability across irregular surfaces, including rocky terrain and slopes.

Our interactive simulation demonstrates how the robot can move across the terrain while generating a digital hazard grid that classifies areas as Safe, Caution, or Danger.

ORVEX also applies physics and mechanical principles, including gravitational forces, friction, torque, ground reaction forces, contact pressure, and stability analysis.

These calculations help estimate terrain accessibility and support intelligent route planning.

When the simulated ground assessment identifies an unexpected hazard, the system demonstrates dynamic route replanning to identify an alternative path.

Technologies, Hardware, and Software

Our team developed both a physical robotic prototype and an interactive web application.

The hardware includes an Arduino Mega microcontroller, 18 servo motors, two ultrasonic distance sensors, a custom-designed and assembled PCB, a 3D-printed robotic body, articulated legs, and integrated electronic components.

The software development involved HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web application, Three.js for interactive 3D visualization, and Arduino IDE with C++ for robotic programming.

We also integrated NASA Mars Trek planetary imagery, implemented physics-based calculations, developed interactive mission dashboards, and deployed our platform using Vercel.

The platform supports both English and Arabic and provides interactive exploration, simulation, mission planning, and reporting features.

What Makes ORVEX Innovative?

Unlike conventional mapping interfaces, ORVEX combines NASA orbital intelligence, robotic ground verification, and physics-based decision support in one integrated system.

NASA's planetary imagery provides the scientific and geographical context for exploration.

Our physically developed HEX-01 prototype introduces a practical approach to investigating terrain conditions that orbital observations alone may not fully reveal.

The physics-based simulation combines mechanical calculations, hazard visualization, and route replanning to demonstrate how exploration decisions could be improved.

Our innovation is not simply a Mars map or an exploration robot. It is an integrated concept connecting orbital observations, robotic exploration, and astronaut safety.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ORVEX aims to reduce exploration risks, improve mission planning, support scientific investigations, and increase the efficiency of future Mars surface operations.

The project demonstrates how accessible robotic hardware, open scientific data, and modern web technologies can be combined to develop advanced space-exploration solutions.

During development, our team considered astronaut safety, Martian gravity, uneven terrain, robot stability, energy efficiency, scientific objectives, data reliability, and interface accessibility.

Current Development and Future Vision

We have developed a physical HEX-01 prototype and a working interactive web platform that displays NASA orbital imagery and demonstrates robotic movement, hazard classification, physics calculations, and route replanning.
